A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sMBR research, with matching methods and retained experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables, and all appendices are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation experiments, source-quality and sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LLM translation experiments, epsilon-sampling results, and a QE-reranking runtime measurement.

M1.justification: The practical decoding procedure remains unchanged: average QE utilities over original and synthetic sources, using back-translation or paraphrasing. TowerInstruct and the Chinese mT5 generator instantiate existing component roles for additional experiments; no new decoding step or training objective is introduced.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates En→De and En→Ru on newstest2020. v2 retains this coverage and adds generaltest2023 evaluation for three directions, including Zh→En, plus Chinese paraphrase-training data. This substantially extends the represented evaluation data and source-language coverage.

E2.justification: Translation-quality comparisons retain the same MAP, MBR, and QE-reranking comparators. The runtime comparison expands from MBR, MBR-fast, and sMBR-PP in v1 Section 5.4 to include QE reranking in v2 Appendix F. Newly cited efficient MBR methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 replaces COMET/BLEURT evaluation with XCOMET-XXL/MetricX-XXL while retaining BLEU. New experiments use zero-shot TowerInstruct-13B with 128 candidates, versus 400 in the retained classic setup. Epsilon sampling at 0.02 is added for translation-candidate generation; v1 used it only for generating paraphrases.

E4.justification: Figure 3 extends candidate-count sensitivity analysis to epsilon sampling, and source-count analyses receive results under the replacement metrics. Appendix F adds the timing comparison with QE reranking. Existing source-diversity, semantic-similarity, and original-source QE analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use paired bootstrap resampling, significance thresholds of 0.05 and 0.01, and explicitly omit multiple-testing correction. Runtime reporting retains means over five runs. No new uncertainty-reporting practice or explicit increase in repeated runs is introduced.

E6.justification: Classic BLEU table values are retained, but neural-metric results are replaced. For high-resource En→De in Table 1, v1 favors full MBR on COMET and sMBR-PP on BLEURT; v2 favors sMBR-PP on XCOMET (95.19 versus 94.29) and MetricX (1.05 versus 1.29). Tables 2 and 8–10 add LLM and epsilon-sampling outcomes. These are new evaluations, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 replace the candidate-conditioned source distribution P(X|y=h) with P(X|Y), removing v1's explicit approximation footnote. This revises the formal sampling assumption while retaining the practical generation procedure. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the headline claim from being competitive with standard MBR to outperforming it, extending the empirical claim to classic and LLM settings. They also remove fewer utility calls and linear scaling from the advertised advantages. Section 4.2 nevertheless describes LLM performance against MBR as competitive.

C2.justification: v2 introduces the interpretation that better LLM support hypotheses improve standard MBR's utility approximation. It explains the replacement metrics' intended independence, acknowledges remaining training-data overlap, and explicitly connects weak QE models to failure of the utility-proxy assumption. Existing explanations of source diversity and source-phrasing sensitivity remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E add Chinese mT5-large training details, Tower-generated paraphrase pairs, a Chinese embedding filter with threshold 0.925, and LLM decoding with bfloat16 on four H100 GPUs. Existing English-generator and low-resource training details are retained. Both versions still promise code release only after acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Tower, XCOMET, MetricX, and mT5, plus a brief discussion citing confidence-based pruning, reference aggregation, and centroid-based efficient MBR. The Pu et al. BLEURT reference is removed. The central positioning as source-only MBR remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing and reorganization concentrate on the experimental narrative, now divided into classic and LLM setups. The efficiency discussion moves from Section 5.4 to Appendix F, and classic setup details move to Appendix D. Abstract and conclusion wording and several headings change, while the overall section structure and much explanatory prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial LLM and epsilon-sampling tables and expands Figure 3 from nine to twelve panels with replacement metric axes. Tables gain metric-direction arrows, the Self-BLEU caption is corrected, and Figure 2 and existing analysis tables are relocated. The overall two-column style remains.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation through metrics less directly tied to the optimized utility and experiments extending beyond classic English-source systems to LLMs and Chinese sources. Added runtime comparison and sharper limitations clarify practical costs and residual evaluation bias. The abstract and conclusion overgeneralize superiority over MBR despite mixed LLM results, but this weakness does not outweigh the stronger evaluation supporting the paper.
